observed: After the outbox enqueue callback fails, one raw event remains persisted while the origin sequence has not advanced. A subsequent capture fails with CONFLICT.
root_cause: Event acceptance, outbox creation, and sequence advancement are separate operations, not one transaction.
next_test: Persist event, origin sequence and enabled-sync outbox reference atomically, or prove an explicitly approved equivalent recovery protocol; both failure-injection probes must pass.

observed: When localStorage reads work but writes fail, the second capture reuses a committed origin sequence and conflicts. When storage is null, successive origin lookups return different UUIDs.
root_cause: readSeq returns 0 for an absent stored value rather than the retained memory sequence; optional storage access does not throw, so null storage creates a new origin instead of using the fallback.
next_test: Cover read-only/quota-blocked/missing storage and stable per-session identity without silently resetting committed sequence state.

observed: Eight concurrent accept calls on one adapter produced one success and seven ENOENT rename errors in the recorded reproduction; source appends race with a shared temporary sidecar path.
root_cause: No acceptance serialization; each call reads an old index and writes the same index.json.tmp.
priority: Resolve before allowing concurrent JSONL use
next_test: Concurrent writes and exact retries must preserve every acknowledged event and unique monotonic receipts, including multiple adapter instances or an explicitly enforced single-writer boundary.

category: JSONL same-count corruption is not detected
observed: Reversing two index entries without changing their count made read(learner:a) return learner:b evidence. A changed raw body was also returned despite its stale stored fingerprint.
root_cause: load checks only event/index lengths and coarse index shape, then joins events to entries by array position.
priority: Fail closed before reading corrupted storage
next_test: Validate identity, learner/origin linkage, fingerprint and sequence invariants before read/getById/accept. This is a synthetic local corruption test, NOT a report of live data leakage.

observed: Concurrent identical accepts returned CONFLICT or IntegrityError instead of DUPLICATE. The deterministic two-connection interleaving yielded one ACCEPTED and one UNIQUE-constraint IntegrityError.
root_cause: The ID/origin checks and insertion are not enclosed in an early write transaction or a conflict-safe reselect path.
next_test: Use real concurrent SQLite connections; exact retries must yield one ACCEPTED and all remaining DUPLICATE without losing the immutable event. A19 pauses after real SELECT results; no DB outcomes are mocked.

category: Direct store acceptance does not enforce the evidence contract
requirement: Spec 27.1 explicitly requires supported schema, definition, context, payload, privacy and producer checks in adapter-equivalent semantics
observed: All three store APIs accepted and persisted schema_version=999 plus an undeclared mastery field.
root_cause: The direct persistence APIs fingerprint/write without the envelope and governance checks applied by the constructor/HTTP endpoint.
priority: Resolve contract boundary before adding more producers
next_test: Reject unsupported schema/derived truth on every governed store entry path, or obtain an explicit reviewed contract decision that defines a validated-only storage boundary. Control A11 confirms the current HTTP endpoint DOES reject these inputs; this finding is not an HTTP validation bypass.

observed: Authorized GET requests with an oversized positive after_store_seq returned HTTP 500 rather than an explicit client-input rejection.
root_cause: Positive Python integers are passed to SQLite without checking its representable cursor range.
next_test: Reject out-of-range cursor values with a defined 400/422 contract; preserve default-deny authorization.

category: SQLite schema does not fully match approved query-column contract
observed: Nine specified separate columns are absent: domain_id, form_id, item_interaction_id, locale, mode, objective_id, occurred_at, question_family_id, track_id.
root_cause: The implemented table/index contract is narrower than the approved logical-column list.
priority: Specification/conformance gap, not proven data loss
next_test: Implement an additive, migration-tested query-column contract or formally reconcile the specification. These values may still exist inside event_json; the audit does NOT claim their raw values were erased.

observed: A persisted schema-valid DELETED record whose predecessor is absent was returned as a completed outcome.
root_cause: records validates individual schemas; propagation follows descendants and returns a terminal record without proving the ancestor chain.
next_test: Validate roots, predecessors, identity and lifecycle continuity before reporting a completed deletion. Normal append paths already check predecessor transitions; this finding specifically concerns inconsistent persisted history.
